headline: Six months of low magnesium
body: Thinner plates. Disordered columns. Less matrix.
punch: And the animals weighed the same as controls.

headline: That last detail
body: If body weight had dropped, this would just be malnutrition slowing everything down. It didn't. The deficit was specific to cartilage.

headline: The restriction
body: Ten percent of nutrient requirement, for six months. Not an extreme deprivation model — a sustained partial shortfall.
punch: The kind of gap a real diet can produce.

headline: What broke
body: Disordered chondrocyte column formation, thinner growth plates, reduced articular chondrocyte density, and reduced extracellular matrix proteoglycan.
punch: Columns are how a growth plate produces length. They stopped lining up.

headline: And the marker
body: Sox9 immunolocalisation was reduced in both growth plate and articular chondrocytes — Sox9 being the master transcription factor for chondrocyte identity.
punch: The cells lost the signal telling them what to be.

headline: Why this deserves attention
body: Magnesium insufficiency is common, cheap to correct, and carries no adverse-effect profile at dietary levels. Very little else in this topic has that combination.
punch: Common deficiency. Trivial fix. Specific mechanism.

headline: But be careful
body: This is a rat deficiency model. It shows what a shortfall damages. It does not show that supplementing beyond adequacy does anything at all.
punch: Fixing a deficit is not the same as adding a surplus.

headline: Which is the general rule
body: Deficiency studies tell you what happens below the line. They are routinely quoted as if they showed benefit above it. They don't.
punch: Below adequate is a problem. Above adequate is a separate question.
